# 02 · Emberford, the Home City (SEALED — "Common knowledge" blocks are player-safe)

> **Emberford** (aka Ember Ford, Emberforde, "the Ford"). Pop. ~65,000. The great river city of the Midriver, built on islands and hills where the Tamber splits around the old shallow ford. The city of lamps, where magic is part of everyday life.

## At a glance

- **Sound and look:** warm stone, slate roofs, bridges everywhere, and thousands of **glimmer lamps**: little glass globes holding a chip of pale-blue crystal that glows when tapped and stays lit for a month. Lamps hang on every corner, every barge, every tavern sign. The city never goes fully dark.
- **Smells:** river mud, bread, tannery lye in the Fringe, hot metal on Enchanters' Row, frying fish at the Wharves.
- **Magic feels normal:** heat-stones in poor kitchens, a warm-coat charm sewn into a dockhand's collar, self-stirring pots in taverns, flying message-moths for 1 cp a note, singing doorbells. Most of it runs on glimmer.
- **Motto** (carved over the Guildhall): *"Every hand a light."*

## Government: The Guild Concord

Emberford is a **guild republic**. No lord, no king's governor. The crown in Highmarch gets taxes and gets left alone.

- **Nine Great Guilds** each send their Guildmaster to the **Concord**, which meets in the Guildhall on Guildhall Isle.
- The Concord elects a **Provost** for 5 years: the city's chief executive, judge of last appeal and voice to the crown.
- **Current Provost:** **Margery Teague** (aka Margie, Marjorie Teeg), Guildmaster of the Bargemen and Porters. Gruff, honest, overworked, distrusts "lamp people." Re-election is this coming Harvest (a political backdrop for Act I).
- Everyone who isn't in a guild has little real say, which is most of the Fringe.

| Guild | Guildmaster (Tier 2–3) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bargemen and Porters | Margery Teague (also Provost) | Biggest guild, muscle of the city |
| Merchants and Factors | Osric Vane (aka Ozrick Vain) | Money; quietly jealous of the Enchanters |
| **Enchanters** | **Hollis Grane** | Richest guild; controls glimmer supply and licenses |
| Lamplighters | Dorcas Fell (aka Dorkas) | Maintain and recharge city lamps; tied to the Enchanters |
| Smiths and Wrights | Big Tam Hollin | Honest, loud, Gideon's sometime employer |
| Brewers and Vintners | Widow Agnes Brack | Runs half the taverns; sponsors festivals |
| Weavers and Dyers | Lionel Hartley | Fashion, Crownhill money |
| Masons | Garrick Stone | Bridges, walls; knows every tunnel |
| Physicians and Apothecaries | Doctor Prudence Ames | Licenses healers; would love to shut Moss's shop |

## Law: The Ford Watch (light presence)
- About 300 watchmen for the whole city: one watch-house per district, a jail on Temple Isle ("the Cage").
- **Captain of the Watch:** **Captain Roderick Hale** (aka Rod, Roddy Hale). Practical, tired, takes small bribes for small things, will not sell out a murder.
- The Watch patrols Crownhill, Guildhall Isle and the markets. They barely touch the Fringe and the Wharves.
- **How law really works:** guilds police their own; Crownhill hires private guards (Gideon's trade); the Wharves answer to the dockmasters; the Fringe takes care of itself.
- **Punishments:** fines, the stocks on Market Steps, a night in the Cage, labor on the river dredges. Hanging only for murder and treason. Theft gets a fine or a flogging. Theft from a guild gets the guild's own justice, which is worse.
- **Bounty board** outside each watch-house: small-time bounties, 5–50 gp.

## Districts

### Crownhill (noble and guild-rich)
The tall hill on the east bank. White stone townhouses, walled gardens, private glimmer fountains, guards at gates. The Grane townhouse, the Provost's residence, Brightwell & Daughters (luxury magic shop), the Weavers' showrooms, the Crownhill Assembly Rooms (balls and auctions).
- *Worth stealing:* everything. Hard to get to: private guards, ward-chimes, dogs.
- *Jobs:* nobles hire off the books for retrieval, "discreet escort," blackmail recovery, finding runaway heirs.

### Guildhall Isle and Temple Isle (the Islands)
Two islands in the Fordwater, joined to the banks by the **Seven Bridges**.
- **Guildhall Isle:** the great domed Guildhall (Concord chamber, guild vaults, the Enchanters' private wing and *deep cellars*, see DM notes), the Exchange, the Hall of Records.
- **Temple Isle:** the Temple of the Bright Lady (see 07), the Cage (jail), the Ford Watch headquarters, the city orphan-house **Lamp House** run by **Hester Grane**.

### The Commons
The big working district on the west bank. Smiths, coopers, bakers, chandlers, tenements, small temples, crowded taverns. Busy and loud. Most of the city lives here.
- Notable: **The Hammer and Hops** (smiths' tavern), **Tam Hollin's forge**, the **Commons Watch-house**.

### Market Steps
A long stair-street of terraces running from the Commons down to the river. Every terrace is a market: fish, cloth, spice, junk, pets, books.
- **Odd Lot** (junk-magic pawnshop), the **Bone Table** (dice game run under an awning), the stocks, street performers, the knife-throwing wall.
- The main gathering place. News travels here first.

### The Wharves (docks)
The long riverfront below Market Steps and along the Low Wharf. Barges, warehouses, sailors, porters, gulls.
- **Mother Brine's** (potion and remedy shop, the sailor's choice), the **Wharfmaster's Office** (job board), **The Drowned Lantern** tavern, **the Bucket** (underground fight ring, see below), Warehouse Row, the Lamplighters' Glimmer Store.
- Rough but friendly to anyone who works.

### Glimmerway (the magic district)
On the west bank between the Commons and Old Ford. Narrow lanes under glass awnings. Always humming.
- **Enchanters' Row** (see 06-magic-and-trade.md): the famous lane of commission workshops.
- **The Lyceum of the Lamp**: the city's college of arcane study (Zeke's school when the family can pay). Old red-brick quads, a crooked tower, a library with a moving staircase.
- **The Patient Owl** (old scholar's magic shop), **The Clockwise** (gnome tinker shop), **The Iron Kettle** (dwarf-run arms-and-armor enchantment, just on the Commons edge).

### Old Ford
The oldest walled district, inside the West Gate, where the city began. Crooked half-timbered houses, a mossy old chapel, the **Ford Stone** (a worn standing stone in the square, where couples swear and children make wishes). Quiet, poor-genteel, full of old people.
- **DM:** The Hall of Two Rivers lies beneath Old Ford. The Ford Stone is its capstone. It hums faintly at the turn of light (seed).

### The Fringe (the outskirts) — HOME
Outside the old city wall, beyond the **West Gate**, where the city spills into garden plots, tanneries, rope-walks, small wooden houses and willow-lined lanes along a slow side-channel called **the Bend**. Poor, tight-knit, proud. It's not in any guild district, so the Fringe takes care of itself.
- **Willow Lane**: the brothers' street. A crooked lane of about twenty houses running down from the West Gate road to the Bend. Willows, chickens, washing lines, a communal well, children everywhere.
  - **The Fenwick house:** a narrow, tall, slightly leaning three-story wooden house at the bottom of the lane near the water. It was the parents' house. Gideon has kept up the rent-tax on it for 18 years. Creaky stairs, a rooftop hatch (Ash's way in and out), Zeke's attic workshop full of half-built gadgets, Gideon's neat room with his sword on pegs.
  - **Moss's shop:** **The Green Jar** (herbs, remedies, teas, poultices), halfway up the lane. Bunches of drying herbs, jars to the ceiling, a cat, and a grumpy assistant at the counter. Moss lives above it.
  - **The Lane Well:** the communal well, where gossip lives.
  - **The Willow** (aka "the Crooked Willow"): a hunchbacked little tavern at the top of the lane by the road. The neighborhood's living room.
- **The Bend:** the side-channel at the bottom of the Fringe. Fishing, swimming, eel traps, a rotting old barge kids play in.
- **Tanner's Row:** stinking tannery yards east of Willow Lane. Work for anyone strong.
- **The Rope-walk:** a long shed where rope is made. Ash's old hiding place.
- Beyond the Fringe: the **Westwood Road** out through orchards and into the old **Fordwood**, a stretch of woods where Moss goes "gathering" every morning.
  - **DM:** the **Ford Pool** (Emberford's main working Wellgate) lies deep in the Fordwood. Moss tends it daily.

## Festivals and customs

| When | Festival | What happens | Hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Highwater (mid-spring) | **Highwater Fair** | River floods its banks a bit; fair on Market Steps; the **Bargerace** (poled-barge race through the Seven Bridges) | Contest, betting, sabotage |
| Midsummer's Eve | **Turn of Light** | At sunset, everyone floats a tiny glimmer lamp down the river and makes a wish. Lovers kiss on the bridges. | Ash's birthday. A Wellgate-adjacent night: strange things happen at sunset |
| Harvest | **Provost Election** | Guild parades, speeches, bribery, brawls | Political jobs |
| 1st of Leaffall | **Ford Festival** | City founding. The Provost re-lights the Ford Stone lamp. Pageant of the "First Crossing" (a garbled folk memory of the Sundering) | Huge seed opportunity |
| Last night of the year | **Lantern Night** | Every lamp lit, all night. Gift-giving: small enchanted trinkets are the customary gift | Gifts from Enchanters' Row |
| Every 10th day | **Tenth-day market** | Big market, cheap goods, pickpocket heaven | |

**Customs any local knows:**
- Tap a lamp twice for luck before a trip.
- Never blow out someone else's lamp. It's an insult, close to a curse.
- On Willow Lane, if someone leaves something on your step, you don't ask.
- The "Lamp-oath": swearing on a lit lamp is binding in guild court.
- People touch the Ford Stone for luck before weddings, contests and journeys.

## Side-activity menu (Emberford)

### Contests
- **The Bargerace** (Highwater Fair): team of 4 poling a barge through the Seven Bridges. Skill challenge (Athletics, Acrobatics, Vehicles (water)). Prize 100 gp and a guild ribbon.
- **The Lamp-Climb** (Ford Festival): climb the greased 60-foot Great Lamp pole on Guildhall Isle and tap the lamp. Prize 50 gp and a free drink in every tavern for a year (in theory).
- **Knife Wall** (Market Steps, any day): throw five knives at painted targets, 1 sp a try. Weekly champion gets 10 gp.
- **The Riddle Table** (the Lyceum, monthly): students and townsfolk answer riddles; a minor magic item prize. Zeke's favorite.
- **Liars' Night** at The Willow (monthly): best tall tale wins the tab.
- **Guild Games** (Harvest): strength, archery, wrestling, tug-of-war between guilds. Outsiders can enter as "Fringe" team.

### Fight rings
- **The Bucket:** underground ring in a drained cistern under a Wharves warehouse. Bare-knuckle, cudgels, sometimes "beast bouts." Run by a big quiet woman called **Ma Garrow** (aka Garo). Entry 5 gp; purses 20–200 gp. Rules: no weapons that cut, no magic, "no killing on a Tenth-day." Betting is huge.
- **Street fights:** informal, behind The Drowned Lantern, settled with a crowd and a hat for coins.

### Betting
- The Bone Table (dice, Market Steps), Kings and Ferrymen (card game at The Willow and the Drowned Lantern), Bargerace books, fight-ring books, election odds.

### Odd jobs (Ash's bread and butter)
- **Courier runs** (message, parcel, "don't-open-it" package): 2–20 gp.
- **Retrieval:** find a lost ring, a stolen dog, a debt-ledger, an heirloom pawned without permission: 10–100 gp.
- **Minor bounties** (Watch board): skip-bail debtors, a pickpocket gang, river rats (literal and figurative): 5–50 gp.
- **Guard and escort** (Gideon's line): 2–10 gp/night.
- **Test subject** at the Lyceum (Zeke's line): 5 gp and possibly a new hair color.
- **Wharf work:** loading, 1 gp/day.

### Things worth stealing
- A Crownhill merchant's ledger proving he's starving out Fringe tenants.
- The Weavers' Guild's prize "Dawnsilk" bolt.
- A visiting noble's glimmer-sapphire.
- Enchanters' Guild shipping manifests (DM: these reveal glimmer volumes far beyond what the city uses, which is a seed).
- Pawned keepsakes from Odd Lot (to give back to their owners).

### Rivals
- The **street rival** and his crew (named in the Truth File) work the same streets.
- **Lyceum snobs** who look down on Zeke.
- A rival courier outfit, **Swift and Sons**, who undercut Ash's prices.
- A rival bouncer at the Drowned Lantern who hates Gideon.

## Common knowledge (player-safe summary for the packet)
- Emberford is ruled by the Guild Concord. The Provost is Margery Teague, the bargemen's boss. The richest guild is the Enchanters', led by kind old Master Hollis Grane, who pays for lamps in poor streets and scholarships at the Lyceum.
- The Ford Watch is small and mostly guards the rich. Out in the Fringe, people sort things out themselves.
- Glimmer lamps come from glimmerstone, a crystal the Enchanters' Guild mines from "deep springs" somewhere outside the city and refines in Glimmerway.
- Local heroes: **Provost Teague** (fought river pirates in her youth), **Hester Grane** (runs Lamp House orphanage, has fed half the Fringe), **"Old Bram"** the ferryman who pulled forty people from the river in the Great Flood of YF 1079.
- People everyone avoids: **Ma Garrow** at the Bucket; the **Tolley brothers**, debt collectors for the Merchants' Guild; the masked "lamp-wardens" who guard Enchanters' Guild shipments; and the Fordwood after dark.
- Recent rumors (spring YF 1104): a hare-folk was seen at the Wharves (people laughed); lamps flicker at sunset in Old Ford; glimmer prices went up again; a Lyceum student went missing.

## DM notes (sealed)
- **The Guildhall's deep cellars** hold the Enchanters' **Grand Reserve**: a vast store of raw glimmer, being "tuned" into a single resonance by Clara's Voice. Hollis's plan: overload it on Lantern Night to crack the Emberford seal from beneath. Act I/II climax material.
- **Lamp House** (Hester's orphanage) is genuine kindness. Hollis also uses it to find grieving or lost children who "hear things" (seed: a kid there hums Ash's tune).
- **Glimmer mines:** the Guild's main "deep spring" mine is the **Kessel Workings**, a quarry-cave a half-day upriver, built around a minor Wellgate. Guarded by lamp-wardens.
- **The Lyceum's crooked tower** has a sealed upper room with a Sundering-era mural (seed for Zeke's discovery).
- **The Ford Stone** hums at the turn of light. Ash can hear it. No one else can. (seed)
